source_title: India ready to share battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners: Rajnath

In this screengrab from a video received on October 29, 2026, Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh addresses the 13th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Defence Ministers’ Meeting. | Photo Credit: PTI
India is committed to collective regional security and the eradication of terrorism in all its forms and is ready to share its battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners to strengthen joint capabilities, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Thursday (October 29, 2026).
Addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines, Mr. Singh said India’s counter-terrorism experience was not theoretical knowledge but had been acquired through decades of confronting complex security challenges, including cross-border terrorism.
He said India’s strategies had been tested and refined through real-world operations, with Operation Sindoor demonstrating the country’s proactive counter-terrorism doctrine.
During the operation, India dismantled terrorist infrastructure and enforced a firm red line against state-sponsored terrorism, he said.
Emphasising that terrorism knows no borders, Mr. Singh said India was prepared to share its operational experience with ADMM-Plus partners through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes and intelligence sharing.
Counter-terrorism remains an important area of cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework, with India and Malaysia co-chairing the Experts’ Working Group on Counter-Terrorism for the 2024-2027 cycle.
In a significant proposal to deepen regional engagement, Mr. Singh called for the establishment of a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ to strengthen institutional people-to-people connectivity between India and ASEAN countries. The ASEAN members appreciated the move of establishing ‘Youth Bridge’.
The initiative would promote digital innovation and capacity building, while providing greater opportunities for young people to contribute to regional peace and security. The proposal was appreciated by ASEAN members.
Highlighting the importance of maritime security, Mr. Singh said India had designated 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation and had conducted the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He reiterated India’s commitment to freedom of navigation, international maritime law and the security of global sea lanes.
Pointing to the Indian Navy’s uninterrupted operational presence in the Gulf of Aden since 2008, he said India had escorted thousands of merchant vessels and thwarted dozens of hijacking attempts, irrespective of the vessels’ flag or nationality.
He reaffirmed India’s commitment to ASEAN centrality and a free, open, inclusive and rules-based Indo-Pacific, adding that New Delhi would continue to serve as a reliable net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and the wider Indo-Pacific.

hi_body:
केंद्रीय रक्षा मंत्री राजनाथ सिंह ने गुरुवार (29 अक्टूबर, 2026) को कहा कि भारत सामूहिक क्षेत्रीय सुरक्षा और आतंकवाद के सभी रूपों को समाप्त करने के लिए प्रतिबद्ध है। उन्होंने कहा कि देश अपने युद्ध-परीक्षित आतंकवाद-रोधी अनुभव को आसियान (ASEAN) भागीदारों के साथ साझा करने के लिए तैयार है ताकि संयुक्त क्षमताओं को मजबूत किया जा सके।

फिलीपींस के सेबू में 13वें आसियान रक्षा मंत्री बैठक-प्लस (ADMM-Plus) को संबोधित करते हुए, श्री सिंह ने बताया कि भारत का आतंकवाद-रोधी ज्ञान सैद्धांतिक नहीं है, बल्कि सीमा पार आतंकवाद सहित जटिल सुरक्षा चुनौतियों का सामना करते हुए दशकों में अर्जित किया गया है। उन्होंने उल्लेख किया कि 'ऑपरेशन सिंदूर' ने भारत के सक्रिय आतंकवाद-रोधी सिद्धांत को प्रदर्शित किया, जिसके तहत आतंकवादी ढांचों को ध्वस्त किया गया।

## प्रमुख प्रस्ताव और क्षेत्रीय सहयोग

* **परिचालन सहयोग:** भारत ने संयुक्त अभ्यास, क्षमता निर्माण कार्यक्रमों और खुफिया जानकारी साझा करने के माध्यम से अपने अनुभव साझा करने की पेशकश की।
* **कार्य समूह की सह-अध्यक्षता:** एडीएसएम-प्लस ढांचे के तहत आतंकवाद-रोधी सहयोग जारी है, जिसमें भारत और मलेशिया 2024-2027 चक्र के लिए विशेषज्ञों के कार्य समूह की सह-अध्यक्षता कर रहे हैं।
* **रक्षा 'यूथ ब्रिज':** श्री सिंह ने भारत और आसियान देशों के बीच संस्थागत लोगों से लोगों के संपर्क को मजबूत करने के लिए एक समर्पित रक्षा 'यूथ ब्रिज' स्थापित करने का प्रस्ताव रखा, जिसे आसियान सदस्यों द्वारा सराहा गया।

## समुद्री सुरक्षा और इंडो-पैसिफिक प्रतिबद्धता

समुद्री सुरक्षा के महत्व को रेखांकित करते हुए, श्री सिंह ने कहा कि भारत ने वर्ष 2026 को आसियान-भारत समुद्री सहयोग वर्ष के रूप में नामित किया है और दूसरा आसियान-भारत समुद्री अभ्यास आयोजित किया है। उन्होंने नेविगेशन की स्वतंत्रता और अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुद्री कानून के प्रति भारत की प्रतिबद्धता दोहराई।

इसके अलावा, उन्होंने 2008 से अदन की खाड़ी में भारतीय नौसेना की निरंतर परिचालन उपस्थिति का हवाला दिया और कहा कि हजारों व्यापारी जहाजों को सुरक्षा प्रदान की गई है। श्री सिंह ने एक स्वतंत्र, खुले और समावेशी इंडो-पैसिफिक क्षेत्र के प्रति भारत के समर्थन की पुष्टि की।

## सत्यापन और व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ

interested पक्ष और विश्लेषक एडीएसएम-प्लस शिखर सम्मेलन के बाद जारी आधिकारिक रक्षा मंत्रालय की विज्ञप्तियों के माध्यम से मूल घोषणाओं का सत्यापन कर सकते हैं।

en_body:
Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh stated on Thursday (October 29, 2026) that India is committed to collective regional security and ready to share its battle-tested counter-terrorism expertise with ASEAN partners. 

Speaking at the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) held in Cebu, Philippines, Mr. Singh reported that India’s counter-terrorism experience was built through decades of addressing complex security challenges, including cross-border terrorism. He mentioned that strategies had been refined via real-world operations, highlighting Operation Sindoor as an example of India's proactive counter-terrorism doctrine that dismantled terrorist infrastructure and enforced limits against state-sponsored terrorism.

## Key Proposals and Regional Cooperation

* **Operational Collaboration:** India offered to share experience through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes, and intelligence sharing.
* **Working Group Co-Chairmanship:** Counter-terrorism cooperation continues under the ADMM-Plus framework, where India and Malaysia currently co-chair the Experts’ Working Group for the 2024-2027 cycle.
* **Defence 'Youth Bridge':** Mr. Singh proposed establishing a dedicated defence 'Youth Bridge' to enhance institutional people-to-people connectivity, promote digital innovation, and support youth contributions to regional peace. This proposal reportedly received appreciation from ASEAN members.

## Maritime Security and Indo-Pacific Commitment

Mr. Singh emphasized maritime security, noting that India designated 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation and conducted the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He reaffirmed support for freedom of navigation, international maritime law, and global sea lane security.

Furthermore, he cited the Indian Navy's continuous operational presence in the Gulf of Aden since 2008, stating that thousands of merchant vessels had been escorted and hijacking attempts thwarted regardless of vessel flag. Mr. Singh reiterated India's dedication to ASEAN centrality, a rules-based Indo-Pacific, and its ongoing role as a reliable net security provider.
